questions.question: The last Mughal emperor of India was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bahadur Shah II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bahadur Shah II**, also known as Bahadur Shah Zafar, was the last Mughal emperor of India.
 
• He reigned from **1837 to 1857**, until the British formally ended the Mughal Empire after the Revolt of 1857.
 
• Bahadur Shah Zafar was a symbolic leader of the Indian rebellion of 1857, although he had limited control over the uprising.
 
• After the suppression of the revolt, he was exiled to Rangoon (present-day Yangon, Myanmar) by the British in **1858**.
 
• Bahadur Shah Zafar was also a noted poet and is remembered for his contributions to Urdu literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revolt of 1857:**

 
 
• The Revolt of 1857, also known as India's First War of Independence, was a major uprising against British rule.
 
• It was triggered by grievances such as economic exploitation, social and religious interference, and military injustices.
 
• Bahadur Shah Zafar was proclaimed the symbolic leader of the revolt by the rebels.
 
 
 
• **End of the Mughal Empire:**
 
 
• The fall of Bahadur Shah Zafar marked the end of the Mughal Empire, which had ruled India for over three centuries.
 
• The British East India Company formally dissolved the Mughal dynasty after the revolt.
 
 
 
• **Exile to Rangoon:**
 
 
• After the suppression of the revolt, Bahadur Shah Zafar was tried by the British and exiled to Rangoon in 1858.
 
• He spent the rest of his life in exile and died in Rangoon in **1862**.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Bahadur Shah Zafar is remembered for his poetry, which expressed his pain and longing during his exile.
 
• He remains an important figure in Indian history as the last emperor and a symbol of resistance against colonial rule.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal was built by who among the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shah Jahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Taj Mahal was commissioned in 1632 by the Mughal Emperor **Shah Jahan** to house the tomb of his favorite wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• The construction of the Taj Mahal was completed in 1653, employing thousands of artisans and craftsmen.
 
• The Taj Mahal is located on the southern bank of the Yamuna River in the city of Agra, India.
 
• This architectural marvel is renowned for its stunning white marble dome and intricate inlay work with precious stones.
 
• The Taj Mahal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is often regarded as the pinnacle of Mughal architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mughal Architecture:**

 
 
• Mughal architecture is characterized by large bulbous domes, slender minarets at the corners, massive halls, and large vaulted gateways.
 
• It combines elements from Persian, Turkish, and Indian architectural styles.
 
• Examples include the Red Fort, Humayun's Tomb, and the Jama Masjid in Delhi.
 
 
 
• **Shah Jahan:**
 
 
• Shah Jahan was the fifth Mughal Emperor, reigning from 1628 to 1658.
 
• He is also known for commissioning other significant buildings such as the Red Fort in Delhi and the Jama Masjid.
 
• His reign is often considered the golden age of Mughal architecture.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites:**
 
 
• The Taj Mahal was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
 
• World Heritage Sites are landmarks or areas with legal protection by an international convention administered by UNESCO.
 
• They are recognized for having cultural, historical, scientific, or other forms of significance.
 
 
 
• **Yamuna River:**
 
 
• The Yamuna River is one of the major rivers of India and the longest tributary of the Ganges.
 
• It flows through several states including Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi, and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: The grading system used by the Mughals to fix rank, salary and military responsibilities is called ___________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mansabdari system.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mansabdari system:-**

 
 
• ​The Mansabdari system was introduced by Akbar for military administration and for the territorial command to sustain the parts of the army.
 
• The Mansabdari system was taken from the system followed in Mongolia.
 
• The Mughal officers whether Hindus or Muslims were given territorial commands in return for military service.
 
• They had to bring in some fixed number of men-at-arms, horses, and elephants to the field and were rated as per the numbers which were known as Zats. 
 
• 'Zat' shows the number of troops that a mansabdar was expected to maintain, while 'sawar' indicate the actual number of horses under the command of a mansabdar.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Iqta system:-**

 
 
• The Iqta system was provided institutional status by Iltutmish__.
 
• The Iqta System or Iqtadari System was introduced by Shamsuddin Iltutmish of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• It was a powerful instrument for centralization.
 
• It was based on the division of territories between Sultans and Nobility.
 
 
 
• **​Ryotwari system:-**
 
 
• Ryotwari System was introduced by Thomas Munro in 1820.
 
• First Ryotwari System was introduced in Madras.
 
• The principle was the direct collection of land revenue from each individual cultivator by government agents.
 
• The advantages of this system were the elimination of middlemen, 
 
• In this system, the Individual cultivator is called Ryot.
 
• This system was in operation for nearly 5 years.
 
 
 
• **Mahalwari system:-**
 
 
• The Mahalwari system was introduced in 1822 by Holt Mackenzie.
 
• Later, the system was reformed during the period of William Bentick in 1833.
 
• **This system divided the land into Mahals. Sometimes, a Mahal was constituted by one or more villages.**

questions.question: Who among the following Mughal emperors had a great interest in paintings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jahangir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Jahangir**, the Mughal emperor (1605–1627), was a patron of the arts, particularly known for his profound interest in paintings and miniature art.
 
• He established a **royal atelier** where skilled painters like Mansur and Abul Hasan flourished under his patronage.
 
• Jahangir is celebrated for introducing **naturalism** in Mughal paintings, with a focus on lifelike portrayals of flora, fauna, and portraits.
 
• He personally reviewed paintings and showed a keen interest in their details, often rewarding artists for their exceptional work.
 
• The period of Jahangir's rule is considered the **golden age of Mughal painting**, marked by the creation of masterpieces like the "Jahangirnama" illustrations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mughal Miniature Paintings:**

 
 
• Miniature painting is a style of art that flourished under the Mughal Empire, combining Persian, Indian, and European influences.
 
• It emphasized intricate details, vibrant colors, and elaborate compositions.
 
• Popular themes included court life, battles, nature, and portraits.
 
 
 
• **Jahangirnama:**
 
 
• The "Jahangirnama" is the autobiography of Jahangir, detailing his life and reign.
 
• It contains vivid descriptions of his love for art, nature, and justice.
 
• The manuscript is richly illustrated with paintings that showcase the artistic achievements of his time.
 
 
 
• **Ustad Mansur:**
 
 
• One of the most famous painters in Jahangir's court, known for his exceptional depictions of animals and plants.
 
• He was titled "Nadir-al-Asr" (Wonder of the Age) by Jahangir for his naturalistic works.
 
 
 
• **Naturalism in Mughal Art:**
 
 
• Introduced by Jahangir, this style focused on realistic and lifelike depictions of subjects.
 
• It marked a departure from the heavily stylized art of earlier periods, emphasizing close observation of nature.

questions.question: To which position in the Mughal administration under Akbar does Diwan-i-Ala refer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Finance Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term **Diwan-i-Ala** in the Mughal administration referred to the position of the **Finance Minister** under Emperor Akbar.
 
• The Diwan-i-Ala was responsible for overseeing the **empire's revenue system**, including tax collection and resource allocation.
 
• This position was part of the central administrative structure, which Akbar organized under his policy of **centralized governance**.
 
• The role required extensive knowledge of land revenue systems, particularly the **Zabt system**, implemented during Akbar's reign.
 
• One of the most notable individuals to hold this position was **Raja Todar Mal**, who introduced significant reforms in the revenue system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zabt System**: This was Akbar's land revenue system, where the average produce of land was calculated over ten years, and one-third of it was fixed as the state's share.
 
• **Raja Todar Mal**: He was Akbar's trusted Diwan-i-Ala and introduced the **standardized revenue collection system**, which became a model for future administrations.
 
• **Mansabdari System**: Akbar's administrative system categorized officials based on their rank (Mansab) and responsibilities, with the Diwan-i-Ala playing a key role in allocating financial resources to Mansabdars.
 
• **Centralized Administration**: Akbar's governance model divided the empire into provinces (Subahs) with officials such as the **Diwan, Subedar, and Bakshi** to manage various aspects of administration under the central authority.
 
• **Akbar's Reforms**: His administrative reforms, including the appointment of the Diwan-i-Ala, were critical in ensuring the Mughal Empire's financial stability and efficient resource management.

questions.question: In which year did Babur defeat Rana Sanga at Khanua ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1527**__.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** In 1527, Babur defeated Rana Sanga at Khanuwa.

__
 
• ​The battle was fought on 16 March 1527.
 
• The Battle of Khanwa was a decisive battle that helps the establishment of Mughal rule in India.
 
• Babur assumed the title of Ghazi after the victory of this battle.
 
• Khanwa is located 60km west of Agra.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Babur was the founder of the Mughal Empire.

 
 
• He was the first Emperor of the Mughal dynasty who ruled between 1526 to 1530.
 
• He defeated Ibrahim Lodhi in the first battle of Panipat in 1526.
 
• He defeated Mahmud Lodi in the battle of Ghaghra in 1529. Babur died in 1530 in Agra.
 
• He was first buried in Agra, later his mortal remains were moved to Kabul and reburied in Bagh-e Babur in Kabul.
 
• Autobiography of Babur: Baburnama.

questions.question: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) marked the beginning of:

options.text: French East India Company's rule in India
British East India company's rule in India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mughal's Rule in India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **First Battle of Panipat** took place on **April 21, 1526**, between the invading forces of **Babur**, the founder of the Mughal Empire, and the army of the Delhi Sultan **Ibrahim Lodi**.
 
• This battle marked the end of the **Delhi Sultanate** and the beginning of the **Mughal Empire** in India.
 
• Babur's forces, equipped with advanced artillery and superior military tactics, decisively defeated Ibrahim Lodi's forces, despite being heavily outnumbered.
 
• The battle was significant for introducing **gunpowder and field artillery** in Indian warfare, which gave Babur a considerable advantage.
 
• After his victory, Babur established the **Mughal dynasty**, which ruled over India for more than three centuries until the advent of British colonial power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Babur:**

 
 
• Babur was a descendant of **Tamerlane** (Timur) on his father's side and **Genghis Khan** on his mother's side.
 
• He was the ruler of the **Fergana Valley** in Central Asia before he invaded India.
 
• Babur's use of **gunpowder and artillery** in battles was revolutionary and played a crucial role in his military success.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Sultanate:**
 
 
• The Delhi Sultanate was established in the early 13th century and was ruled by several dynasties, including the Slave Dynasty, Khilji Dynasty, Tughlaq Dynasty, Sayyid Dynasty, and Lodi Dynasty.
 
• The defeat of Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat marked the end of the Sultanate.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Mughal Rule:**
 
 
• The Mughal Empire brought about significant developments in **administration, architecture, culture, and art**.
 
• Some of the notable contributions include the construction of the **Taj Mahal**, development of the **Mansabdari system**, and advancements in **literature and painting**.
 
 
 
• **First Battle of Panipat:**
 
 
• The battle was fought near the town of **Panipat**, located in present-day Haryana, India.
 
• The use of superior military technology, including **matchlock guns** and field artillery, gave Babur's forces an edge over Ibrahim Lodi's army.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **First Battle of Panipat** is one of the three major battles fought at Panipat in Indian history. The other two were the **Second Battle of Panipat** (1556) between Akbar and Hemu, and the **Third Battle of Panipat** (1761) between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Durrani.
 
• The victory at Panipat allowed Babur to lay the foundation of the **Mughal Empire** and consolidate his power in northern India.
 
• Babur's memoir, the **Baburnama**, provides detailed accounts of his campaigns, including the First Battle of Panipat.

questions.question: ______ in Gujarat was the emporium of western trade during the Mughal Period.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mughal Emperor Jahangir permitted the English East India Company to establish their factory in 1613 at Surat.
 
• The British East India Company came to India for trade in spices, an important commodity in Europe back then, and as it was used to preserve meat.
 
• Apart from this, they primarily do trading in silk, cotton, indigo dye, tea, and opium.
 
• Mughal emperor Jahangir granted a Farman to Captain William Hawkins permitting the English to erect a factory at Surat in 1613. 
 
• In 1615, Thomas Roe, the Ambassador to James I, got an imperial Farman from Jahangir for trading and establishing factories all across the Mughal empire.
 
• In 1616, the company established its first factory in the south in Masulipattanam.
 
• Soon, the Vijayanagara Empire will also give the company permission to open a factory in Madras and the British company started to eclipse the other European trading companies in their rising power.
 
• The 'East India Company' was formed in 1600.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Jahangir was born to Maryam-uz-Zamani and Akbar on August 30, 1569.
 
• He was named Sultan Muhammad Salim after Shaikh Salim Chishti of Fatehpur Sikri.
 
• Akbar called him Sheik Babu.
 
• After his coronation, he assumed the title of Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir Badshah Ghazi.
 
• Jahangir was the only surviving son of Akbar who after his father’s death ascended the throne in 1604, at the age of 34 years.

questions.question: Which among the following was the son of the Mughal emperor Shahjahan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangzeb.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct answer is Aurangzeb. He was the sixth Mughal emperor and ruled from 1658 to 1707.**

 
 
• Aurangzeb was born on October 24, 1618, as the third son of Shahjahan and Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• He was given the title of "Alamgir" which means "Conqueror of the World".
 
 
 
• **Jahangir was the fourth Mughal emperor **and ruled from 1605 to 1627. He was the son of Akbar and the father of Shahjahan.
 
• **Humayun was the second Mughal emperor **and ruled from 1530 to 1540 and again from 1555 to 1556.
 
 
• He was the son of Babur, the founder of the Mughal dynasty.
 
 
 
• Sikander Lodhi was the ruler of the Delhi Sultanate from 1489 to 1517.
 
 
• He was not a Mughal emperor.
 
 
 
• **Hence, the statement "Aurangzeb was the son of the Mughal emperor Shahjahan" is correct.**

questions.question: Moti Masjid in Agra fort was constructed by which of the following Mughal Emperors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shahjahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shahjahan:**

 
 
• Shahjahan reigned during the peak of Mughal architectural splendor.
 
• He commissioned the Moti Masjid (Pearl Mosque) within the Agra Fort, known for its pristine white marble construction.
 
• His most iconic creation is the Taj Mahal, a testament to his love for his wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• He also significantly redesigned the Agra Fort, adding numerous marble structures.
 
• Shahjahan built the Jama Masjid in Delhi, another architectural masterpiece.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aurangzeb:**

 
 
• Aurangzeb's reign saw a decline in Mughal architectural patronage.
 
• While he did construct the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore, his focus shifted more towards military campaigns and expanding the empire.
 
• His architectural style was less ornate than that of Shah Jahan.
 
• Aurangzeb's rule is often characterized by its strict adherence to Islamic law.
 
• His rule expanded the Mughal empires territory to its largest size.
 
 
 
• **Jahangir:**
 
 
• Jahangir was known for his love of art and gardens.
 
• He continued the construction of Akbar's tomb in Sikandra.
 
• He significantly contributed to the development of Mughal painting.
 
• Jahangir also designed many beautiful gardens.
 
• His rule was known for relative peace, and prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Akbar:**
 
 
• Akbar's architectural style blended Persian and Indian influences.
 
• He built the Agra Fort, although Shahjahan later modified it extensively.
 
• He also constructed the city of Fatehpur Sikri, including the Buland Darwaza and Panch Mahal.
 
• He was known for his religious tolerance.
 
• Akbar's rule consolidated the Mughal Empire.
